failure_analysis.what_failed: The fixed-recipe supervisor only rescales the nominal setpoints with the production target and never reacts to disturbances. Feed draw-off from tank1, pump-gain loss or split-valve shifts drove pump 2 (the h1 loop) to saturation, lifting h3 hundreds of seconds above the 0.75 m limit while production stayed near target.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: If residual upper-level violations remain after this structural model, add an online estimator of gamma1 and gamma2 (or a slow integral trim on the h1/h2 split) so split-valve shifts are treated as accurately as feed and pump-gain disturbances.

self_check: Every call the supervisor fits a steady-state disturbance model to the 50 s window: u1=(1-gamma1)k1 and u2=(1-gamma2)k2 come from the window-integrated tank3/tank4 balances, and the lumped d1,d2 then follow from the tank1/tank2 balances, so the estimate is unbiased even while a pump is saturated. It then sweeps the one-dimensional family of setpoint pairs that meets the production target and predicts h3,h4,v1,v2 from that model, capping any predicted pump voltage at 12 V and recomputing the resulting floating h1 or h2. The chosen pair minimises predicted upper-level/band/safety/pump penalties plus 100 per metre of setpoint travel, so it shifts production toward the unconstrained tank whenever the predicted violation justifies the move, and holds still when no violation is predicted.
proposed_change: Replace the fixed recipe with a steady-state model identified online from the telemetry window and a one-dimensional setpoint search along the production-target curve that trades predicted constraint violations against setpoint travel. Saturated-pump branches recompute the level that the other loop can no longer hold.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The fixed recipe never moves the setpoints, so feed draw-off, pump-gain loss and split shifts raise the required pump voltages: pump2 saturates and h3 climbs past 0.75 m (feed/split/combined) or pump1 saturates and production falls (pump loss), giving long upper-level violations plus production loss, with zero use of the free degree of freedom.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the steady-state predictor but tune the h3/h4 safety margin and the travel-vs-penalty weighting, and add explicit trend/oscillation awareness so setpoints hold through sinusoidal disturbances with less travel.

self_check: The supervisor reconstructs the steady-state flow-to-voltage map at the measured operating point (disturbance folded into an offset) and predicts h3 and h4 for every candidate split of the production target between tank1 and tank2. It then picks the feasible split closest to the active setpoints, so when a disturbance pushes an upper level toward its limit it lowers that tank's setpoint (h1 for h3, h2 for h4) and raises the other to keep Q exactly on target, and when a pump approaches saturation it trims the corresponding lower-tank setpoint to cut the voltage demand. A 3 cm margin under the upper-level limit and a snap-to-active deadband prevent jitter and unnecessary travel, while if no split is feasible it returns the least-violating one.
proposed_change: Replace the fixed recipe with a model-based steady-state supervisor that uses the production degree of freedom to keep h3 and h4 under a safety margin and pumps unsaturated, choosing the feasible split nearest the active setpoints. Disturbance effects are estimated online from the windowed levels/pump voltages so no explicit disturbance model is needed.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor is a frozen recipe: it never uses the free setpoint split, so any disturbance that raises pump-2 voltage (draw-off from tank1, pump-1 gain loss, gamma1 shift) drives h3 through tank3 and over the 0.75 m upper limit for hundreds of seconds (dev_feed_step 853 s, dev_combined_step 588 s). Combined pump/split faults also saturate the pumps (up to 430 s) and let production drift off target because the loops lose authority.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Estimate online the effective (1-gamma)*k coefficients and the two feed disturbances from the 50-sample window via the exact mass balances, then每 call re-optimise the h1/h2 split to minimise production error, h2-band, h3/h4-limit and safety cost plus a setpoint-travel charge.

self_check: Each call the supervisor reconstructs the exact steady-state model from the telemetry window (effective (1-gamma)*k coefficients from the tank3/tank4 balances, and the two unmeasured feed flows from the tank1/tank2 balances with the d h/dt terms), then searches the setpoint pair that minimises production error plus 2-per-second penalties on the h2 band and the h3/h4 limits plus 1-per-metre of setpoint travel. When a disturbance drives h3 up or pump 2 toward 12 V, lowering the h1 setpoint and raising h2 shifts production to tank2, which cuts the pump-2 demand through tank3 and restores h3 headroom while Q stays on target because Q depends only on the two setpoints; the symmetrical move (raise h1, lower h2) is used when h4 or pump 1 approaches its limit. If a limit cannot be held without a large production sacrifice, the optimiser sheds a little production (1 point per L/s) instead of paying 2 points per second of band or upper-limit violation. Steps are rate-limited and a 2.5 mm deadband suppresses jitter so setpoints are moved only when the modelled benefit exceeds the travel charge.
proposed_change: Replace the fixed recipe with an online steady-state optimiser that identifies the effective (1-gamma)*k coefficients and the two feed disturbances from the window and then searches the setpoint pair minimising production error, constraint violations and setpoint travel. The chosen pair is rate-limited and dead-banded before it is returned.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The fixed-recipe supervisor never adapts the h1/h2 split to the active disturbance. With a draw-off on tank1 it keeps h1=0.30, so the h1 loop drives pump2 to the 12 V rail; because pump2 feeds tank3 (tank3 drains into tank1), h3 climbs past 0.75 m for hundreds of seconds (dev_feed_step 853 s, dev_combined_step 588 s). Pump-gain and split faults act the same way, and nothing ever shifts production toward tank2 to relieve pump2.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Estimate the active disturbance from the recent mass balances and solve the steady-state split so setpoints sit on the constant-production curve a1*sqrt(h1)+a2*sqrt(h2)=C while predicted h3/h4 stay under their limits with minimal setpoint travel.

self_check: Each call I estimate the current feed/pump/split disturbance from the tank mass balances using recent level and voltage trends, then search along the constant-production curve for the setpoint pair whose predicted steady pump voltages keep h3 and h4 below a soft limit with the smallest setpoint move. Because h3 is fixed by the tank1 inflow coming from pump2 through tank3, lowering the h1 setpoint (shifting production into tank2) lowers v2 and pulls h3 down while Q stays on target, and the opposite shift protects h4 and h2. A soft margin plus a small deadband stop needless motion, and a pump-saturation penalty pushes production off the offending pump before it rails.
proposed_change: Replace the fixed recipe with a one-dimensional search over the production split f (h1=(f*C/a1)^2, h2=((1-f)*C/a2)^2, C=Q/(1000*sqrt(2g))) using a steady-state model driven by a window-based disturbance estimate. The cost combines setpoint travel with penalties for predicted h3/h4 limit exceedance, h2 band exceedance, safety limits and pump saturation.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The fixed recipe ignores disturbances. A tank-1 draw-off forces the h1 loop to raise pump 2, sending excess flow to tank 3 and violating the upper-level limit. Pump-gain loss or split shifts cause similar pump saturation and upper-level violations because the production split degree of freedom is unused.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Add constraint-driven feedback that shifts the production split only when h3/h4 approach their limit or a pump saturates, rate-limiting setpoint moves and keeping h2 within its band.

self_check: When h3 approaches its limit or pump 2 saturates, I lower the h1 setpoint and raise the h2 setpoint along the constant-production curve, cutting the required v2 and therefore h3. When h4 is high or pump 1 saturates, the opposite shift raises h1 and lowers h2 to reduce v1 and h4. The h2 setpoint is clamped to the h2 band, and all moves are rate-limited so production stays near target without excessive setpoint travel.
proposed_change: Add a constraint-relief shift to the fixed production recipe: h3/pump-2 proximity lowers h1 and raises h2, h4/pump-1 proximity raises h1 and lowers h2, with h2 clamped to its band and rate limits on setpoint motion.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor returned a fixed production-scaled recipe and never exploited the production-split degree of freedom, so feed draw-off, pump-gain loss and split shifts drove tank 3 (and tank 4) above the 0.75 m limit and the pumps into saturation while production drifted and setpoints never moved.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Add online estimation of the split-valve ratios so the h4 prediction stays conservative when gamma shifts, and tune the trust-region size against oscillatory feed disturbances to minimise setpoint travel chattering.

self_check: The supervisor estimates the two lower-tank disturbance residuals and the effective pump gains from measured levels and upper-tank drain flows, then predicts, for each feasible production split, the steady-state pump flows and the resulting h3, h4 and voltages from the flow balance (which does not need pump gains). It selects the split that keeps production on the target curve while holding predicted h3 and h4 below a margin under the 0.75 m limit, keeping h2 in band and predicted voltages below 11.5 V, and it holds the active setpoints when no margin is threatened. Because the chosen point always lies on the Q-target curve, production recovers to target, and because movement is limited to a small trust region per call, setpoint travel and production transients stay small.
proposed_change: Replace the fixed production-scaled recipe with a flow-balance supervisor that estimates disturbances and effective pump gains from the telemetry window and searches the single production-split degree of freedom, trading predicted upper-level, h2-band and saturation-margin violations against setpoint travel. The returned setpoints always lie on the production-target curve, so Q returns to target while h3/h4 margins are restored and pump saturation is avoided.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor is a fixed disturbance-blind recipe: it always returns the nominal setpoints scaled to the target, so it never uses the production-split degree of freedom. When a feed draw-off on tank 1 (d1<0) forces the h1 loop (pump 2) to raise v2, v2 saturates at 12 V and h3 is driven above 0.75 m for hundreds of seconds (dev_feed_step_0: 853 s; dev_combined_step_0: 588 s), which dominates the score. Pump-gain loss/split shifts similarly saturate a pump and push an upper level past the limit.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the fixed recipe with a steady-state model-based supervisor: estimate the effective feed disturbances from the window using the exact tank-1/2 balances plus the level slope, then search the one-dimensional production split that keeps predicted pump voltages below the upper-tank-limit-derived levels and h2 inside its band while penalising setpoint travel.

self_check: The supervisor reconstructs the required pump voltages for every candidate production split along the constant-Q curve, using disturbance estimates computed from the window (exact mass balances plus the numeric level slope), so a plant condition that would saturate a pump or push an upper tank toward 0.75 m is recognised before it happens. The cost function trades the 100/m setpoint-travel penalty against penalties for predicted voltage-limit, band and safety violations, so when h3 approaches its limit the split shifts production from tank 1 to tank 2 (lowering v2), and when pump 1 strains it shifts the other way. If the active setpoints already predict no violation the zero-travel point wins, so nothing moves unnecessarily. Upper-tank limits are enforced via voltage limits derived from the level limit, which also keeps the loops away from 12 V saturation.
proposed_change: Compute the steady-state pump-voltage demands for every candidate production split (h1,h2 on the constant-Q curve) from window-based disturbance estimates, and return the split minimising setpoint travel plus penalties for predicted voltage/band/safety violations. This unloads a straining pump or an upper tank near 0.75 m while holding production on target.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The fixed setpoint recipe ignores disturbances entirely: a step draw-off from tank 1 forces pump 2 to saturation and drives h3 above its 0.75 m limit for hundreds of seconds, and combined pump-gain/split disturbances do the same, because the supervisor never uses the production split degree of freedom to relieve the upper-level constraint.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the steady-state model-based candidate search but make the disturbance estimate and the upper-level margin adaptive to the observed trend of the constraint residuals.

self_check: Each call estimates the two unmeasured feed disturbances by integrating the four tank mass balances over the recent 12 s telemetry window, then solves the steady-state balances for the pump voltages and upper levels at each candidate setpoint pair. The candidate search only visits pairs that satisfy the production target exactly and minimises setpoint travel plus penalties for predicted h3/h4 limit exceedance, h2 band violations and pump saturation, with the current active setpoints included as a candidate so nothing moves needlessly. When a disturbance pushes h3 toward its limit the search lowers h1 (trimming pump-2 demand) and raises h2 to hold Q, and when a pump nears 12 V the measured voltage-bias factor inflates the predicted voltage so the search backs that setpoint down further. A soft margin below the upper-level limit and inside the h2 band gives buffer against model error.
proposed_change: Replace the fixed recipe with a steady-state model-based supervisor that estimates the two feed disturbances by integrating the mass balances over the telemetry window, then searches the constant-production curve for the setpoint pair minimising travel plus penalties for h3/h4 limit, h2 band and pump saturation. The search always returns a pair on the constant-Q curve, so production stays on target while the split protects the upper levels.
